posts.name: starkenburg_alexander
posts.cooked:
Near-Mint
First game was only a loss because I derped and didn't choose CC when she played Missing Resources to probably pull a construct. Instead I lost all of my one-shots, including a ball lightning I was saving to blow up What Doesn't Kill You x2 and Wrathful Retribution. After that I was unable to survive the plink damage AND the retribution damage.

Second game I played the same way execpt I chose CC and didnt lose any cards. Yay me.

 

Basic strategy was "Get Savage Mana and Mere out and keep them out at all costs. Plink away at any target Diversions until Haka can eat them, especially using Temest's XPW base to keep them from doing any damage while out. Tank until she flips, then Ball Lightning her Clues and Wrathful Retribution her face". Worked pretty well when I didnt throw away 3/4ths of my cards. AA and Haka high teens, Tempest and CC sub 10, Fanatic at 1.

Oddly, I found for most of the game that I was using AA's power to actually deal damage to villains as I didnt have any power/plays that I particularly needed.

posts.name: FrivYeti
posts.cooked:
Not a random start, but Miss Info turns random surprisingly quickly thanks to Diversionary Tactics.

My game went very well, though. Thunderstruck kept the Lost Cat out to prevent Miss Info from multi-playing, and I was able to keep her Diversion count at just the one by wiping the rest. I also took advantage of the Misplaced Memo to drop the Mechanic to 1 and leave him immortal, to protect other Environment targets, and then have Fanatic redirect all the damage Miss Info wanted her to do to herself back to Miss Info. With Haka protecting the Adept and also reducing damage and healing, my team was pretty beefy. 

Captain Cosmic still got iced midway through, but he was kind of more useful dead than alive. Thanks to his deliberately terrible opening hand, his powers weren't useful and he couldn't keep Constructs out to save his life (literally, in fact).

posts.name: QuirkyDM
posts.cooked:
Fairly easy mint. Sacrosanct Martyr lets Fanatic deal a lot of damage while not hurting herself thanks to her base power. Rebel Yell let Fanatic do that on the first turn even. With a little help from everyone else, none of the diversions lasted more than a turn except one turn and Ground Pound was out. I set up a lot of ongoings and even with M.I.'s card destruction, I had cards to spare. There was enough healing that everyone was in the teens, but manageable. Energy Bracers on Haka let him soak up damage for whomever needed it the most with no real damage done. The environment card that makes destroyed targets return to the bottom of their deck kept the diversions out of play after that. At the end, I purposely diverted damage to Fanatic for a Wrathful Retirbution, but Miss Information was already at 20 by then and there was no real problem at that point.

I definitely made lots of mistakes. Fanatic takes a whole turn of not using her base power to switch targets. Haka protecting Fanatic sometimes got in the way of Sacrosanct Martyr or Rebel Yell and I didn't want to rewind to keep the mint. Tempest's power got used once maybe? All the targets died too fast. But he was good for Ball Lightning to get rid of ongoings as soon as Miss Information flipped.

posts.name: Arthur_Wynne
posts.cooked:
New poster here!

Near Mint, but on the first try. I've never played with any of these variants before, and I have very little experience with AA in general, so there was no way I was getting through all of these power phases without a rewind or two to get all my ducks in a row. XPW Fanatic's power is pretty good it turns out, especially against a villain with so much self-damage!

I actually like Miss Information's deck a lot better than it seems most people do - I don't find it frustrating, but more of an interesting puzzle. But there's no denying that when H=5, it's pretty hard! At least for a Sentinels neophyte like me. So I'm feeling pretty good about my result. (Fanatic at 5 HP, everyone else KO when I finished her with a 23-point Wrathful Retribution - all of the others were wiped in the turn before, and if I had played correctly I probably could have kept everyone alive, but I saw that it would be very hard and that I would get her with Wrathful Retribution unless she got some kind of really silly draw, so I didn't bother trying to go for a better result. Justice was served in the end, and that's what counts, right? ;)
